target_customer: Online merchants, subscription businesses and collection teams in Chile and Mexico that want to accept bank transfer payments
problem: Card payments are costly and manual bank transfer verification is slow; merchants want instant account-to-account payments with automatic reconciliation.
business_model: Usage-based payments API with a fee per transaction; later a payments operating system with recurring payments and business accounts
product_category: Account-to-account payments and open banking API

founders.name: Cristobal Griffero
founders.background_notes: Describes himself as a CS engineer from Chile on the YC page; no education details given.

founders.name: Lukas Zorich
previous_startups: An unnamed earlier startup where he manually verified bank transfers
founders.background_notes: Software engineer from Chile per YC page; the earlier startup is not named.

competitors.name: Khipu
competitors.what: Chilean electronic transfer payments platform; named by TechCrunch as a Chilean competitor
competitors.traction_then: Not found for 2021; a 2026 article says it began about ten years earlier

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting to many banks through scraping and APIs and handling reconciliation is integration heavy but uses known techniques.

defensibility.rationale: Bank integrations, agreements such as the BancoEstado open banking deal, and licenses in Chile and Mexico are slow to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Global players are named as broader A2A competitors by TechCrunch in 2024, while Fintoc grew in Chile and Mexico; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Chile lacked card alternatives and its Fintech Law was establishing open banking; Chilean merchants used transfers heavily. Evidence is the founders' own account and later press.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, informal Spanish addressing the reader as tu, focused on results and trust

branding.community_and_virality: Press on the company is about funding and licenses, not brand; no community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear developer-facing fintech name with regional press, but nothing showing brand-driven growth.

pivots.from: Open banking API and A2A payments
pivots.to: Payments operating system with recurring payments, AI agents and business accounts
pivots.why: Company site and a 2026 Chilean press headline describe the Payments OS plan; exact date not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Fintoc built an account-to-account payments API for Chile and then Mexico, raised a 7 million dollar Series A in April 2024 led by Propel, and says over 1,200 companies use it. It obtained regulatory authorizations in Chile and Mexico and reportedly processed about 350 million dollars monthly in 2025. It remains active and independent, and its main risks are competition from Khipu and global players and regulatory change.
notes: Series A reported by TechCrunch, The Paypers and Contxto. An earlier seed round with Monashees has no stated amount in TechCrunch; a LatamList URL hints at 3 million dollars, unverified and not recorded as a round. CB Insights lists 10.19 million over seven rounds, aggregator only. Competition: no source dated near the 2021 batch was found; Khipu and ETpay were named by TechCrunch in 2024, and Khipu is described in a 2026 article as about ten years old, so it existed before 2021 but the cited source is later than the batch. Founders' education and prior employers were not found. The processing volume claim comes from a Forbes Chile style summary in search results and is self-reported.
